knowledge_gaps: The ten-item cutoff lacks justification from training-history lengths or timestamp gaps. Report the fraction of supervised and validation histories actually affected; ten interactions do not represent a fixed elapsed-time horizon.

Encoding every supervised position as a separate baseline-length window can multiply backbone computation substantially. Complete-example chunking may still leave too many windows in memory; specify window microbatching, loss normalization and a measured runtime feasibility check within the shared budget.

Right-aligning every window can change positional features and dropout realizations. A full-context windowed control should first reproduce baseline evaluation scores where applicable; otherwise the experiment changes more than available context.

Improvement from bounded-context retraining would support that configuration, but would not identify stale-history harm: regularization, positional changes and optimization effects remain alternative explanations. The report also overstates the shortcut argument; an identity shortcut carries its input state, whose historical content depends on preceding blocks.

Originality 2 is reasonable and potential 6 is plausible but speculative. Difficulty 4 may underestimate overlapping-window computation, gradient accumulation and predictor consistency. Exact inherited settings, chunk sizes, checkpoint rules and reproducible qualitative-assessment criteria remain unspecified.
